correctness.rationale: The two critical-contact cubic equations follow by clearing 4p^2 from h(p)=p and h(p)=1-p. Each polynomial has opposite signs at 1/4 and 1/2 and a strictly signed derivative on this interval. The turns map first to 1 or to the specified outer turn, then to the endpoint orbit 1,0,0. Each outer branch covers [0,1]; the two inner branches cover [p,1] or [1-p,1]. Positive-length Markov cylinders are in bijection with paths: a new interior boundary is a turn pulled back through a strictly monotone piece. Old folds cannot disappear under further composition, since close to a fold the image on both sides lies in the same one-sided neighborhood, on which f is strictly monotone. Thus these cylinders count exactly the maximal laps. On vectors constant on the outer and inner branch pairs, the two transition matrices act by [[2,2],[1,2]] and [[2,2],[1,0]], respectively. The all-ones vector lies in this subspace, so these two-dimensional characteristic polynomials give the stated recurrences from n=1 (the full four-dimensional characteristic polynomial alone would not justify cancellation of its z^2 factor). L_1=4 and L_2=14 or 10 give nonzero positive coefficients for the dominant roots. The lap-growth theorem yields the claimed topological entropies.
residual_risks: The supplied checker was not executed. The cited original lap-growth paper was not accessible in the attempted copies; this calculation uses its standard theorem for continuous piecewise strictly monotone interval maps, not a numerical Lyapunov proxy.

value.rationale: Exact entropy at a naturally defined critical contact could be useful as a calibration of the dynamics; the contacts are not arbitrary parameters. But the frozen finding supplies no new calibration point, sharper invariant, or new structural explanation beyond the earlier five-case classification. It repeats precisely two already-derived cases, so no independently valuable remainder was established.
residual_risks: The comparison concerns independent scientific contribution, not the usefulness of a concise case exposition.
